analysis.title: Airbnb: Growth is Back in the Neighborhood
key_insights: Airbnb delivered its strongest quarter in several years in 3Q, with growth accelerating across every region. Nights and Seats Booked grew 16%, the fastest in four years, while GBV grew 21% and revenue grew 19%.
All regions delivered double-digit growth. North America reached its strongest growth in four years and first-time booker growth accelerated to 13%, the highest since early 2022.
DB says Airbnb's acceleration contrasts with slower growth at the global OTAs, so it reflects company-specific execution rather than a broad travel demand improvement.

Reserve Now Pay Later (RNPL) added 3ppt of net nights growth in 3Q versus about 1.5ppt in 2Q. Hotels added less than 1ppt, implying core homes growth of about 12% excluding the direct benefit from these two initiatives.

For 4Q, Airbnb guides to at least low-double-digit nights growth. DB attributes the sequential moderation to a 1 to 2ppt smaller RNPL contribution, about 1ppt of headwind from lapping cancellation-policy and fee initiatives, and about 1ppt from a difficult industry comparison, and views it as initiative timing and comps.

The migration to a 15.5% single host fee is effectively complete and should add about 1% annualized monetization benefit in 2027, though incentives and promotions could offset part of the take-rate upside.

RNPL eligibility should stabilize near half of eligible GBV. The timing distortion to implied take rate and working capital should normalize by next summer, and Airbnb expects FCF margin to return above EBITDA margin in 2027.

Airbnb is expanding hotels geographically and deepening inventory selectively to address more trip use cases. Distribution partnerships such as American Express extend reach to affluent travelers, and partner-supplied services add revenue-share income.

AI is speeding up execution. About 40% of support issues were resolved without a human agent in 3Q, cutting customer-support cost per booking by more than 17%. Early AI search conversion is comparable with traditional search, and users discover services and experiences at more than twice the prior rate.

A verticalized travel agent is planned for 1H27, built first around the homes advantage and then expanded through APIs, MCPs and native supplier integrations. Sponsored listings and loyalty are further back in the development queue.
DB reiterates Buy and raises its price target to $215 from $200, based on about 21x 2027E FCF, a turn higher than before, and sees room for further multiple expansion.

market_movers.rationale: Reiterates Buy and raises target from $200 on accelerating core growth, differentiated supply and an expanding product roadmap. The target rests on about 21x 2027E FCF.

earnings_insights: Airbnb 3Q26 reported results: Nights and Seats Booked +16%, GBV +21%, revenue +19%, first-time booker growth +13%.
4Q26 company guidance: nights growth of at least low-double-digit.
DB's 2027E FCF multiple for ABNB is about 21x, which underpins the $215 target.
risk_factors: Intense competition in the travel industry.
Geopolitical tensions and the broader competitive environment could pressure the share price.
Broader macro uncertainty could create downside for the stock.
Incentives and promotions could offset part of the take-rate upside from the single host fee.
